class.name: TickMultiplayerPeer
class.description: Lets [SceneMultiplayer] (RPCs, [MultiplayerSpawner], [MultiplayerSynchronizer]) use the players' mesh, next to the [TickNetwork] on the same transport. Every player is reached, directly or relayed by the host, which is peer 1 (the server for [SceneMultiplayer]). Get it with [method EnetHostedMeshTransport.get_multiplayer_peer]. It has [constant EnetHostedMeshTransport.MULTIPLAYER_CHANNEL_COUNT] transfer channels and doesn't need the server relay of [SceneMultiplayer]: the transport relays. [b]Host migration:[/b] [SceneMultiplayer] always takes peer 1 for the server, and after a migration nobody is peer 1: [method MultiplayerAPI.is_server] is [code]false[/code] on every player, and the nodes whose multiplayer authority is still 1 (the default) have no authority, so their [code]"authority"[/code] RPCs, [MultiplayerSpawner]s and [MultiplayerSynchronizer]s stop. In [signal host_migrated], give that authority to the new host ([method Node.set_multiplayer_authority]), and ask the transport who hosts ([method EnetHostedMeshTransport.get_host_peer], [method EnetHostedMeshTransport.is_hosting]). The [TickNetwork] moves its own authority by itself. [codeblock] peer.host_migrated.connect(func(old_host: int, new_host: int): for node in get_tree().get_nodes_in_group(&"hosted"): node.set_multiplayer_authority(new_host) ) [/codeblock]

signal.name: host_migrated
signal.description: The host [param old_host] left and [param new_host] hosts the mesh now (see [member EnetHostedMeshTransport.host_migration]). Emitted before [signal MultiplayerPeer.peer_disconnected] for [param old_host].
